fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. God says, “Mark out one road for the sword to come against Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another against Judah into fortified Jerusalem.” Rabbah is the Ammonites' city, sitting at the end of the second road. Two roads, one starting land, and a signpost at the branch. Ezekiel, the prophet, is basically drawing a map with a sword on it.

Nice try, friend, but Gaza isn't on this map. The text names only two destinations: Jerusalem and Rabbah of the Ammonites. Ezekiel only has two roads to mark, and Gaza didn't make the cut. Rabbah is the other road.
Yes, an omen. Verse 21 says the king of Babylon stands at the fork “…to seek an omen…” and then lists the arrows, the idols and the liver. That's a whole lot of effort at one fork in the road.
Not quite, friend. The king of Babylon stands at the junction “…to seek an omen…” The arrows, the idols and the liver are all how he goes about it. A blessing isn't what he's after at that fork.

Yes, guilt. The omen “…will draw attention to their guilt and take them captive.” To those who swore allegiance to the king, it will seem like a false omen. I bet they brush it off, but the text says it draws attention to their guilt anyway.

Actually it's true, friend. The Lord GOD says their sins are revealed in all their deeds, and then He says, “…you shall be taken in hand.” That's right there in verse 24. It's a heavy one, so we can read it slowly.

Yes, final. God says to the profane and wicked prince of Israel, “…the day has come for your final punishment.” Notice the word isn't light and it isn't delayed. It's final, and the day has come. I think this one is heavy.

That's it, baker. God says, “Remove the turban, and take off the crown.” Both of those go on the head, and God gives the order for them to come off. I wear a tall chef's hat, so I'd be nervous if someone told me to take mine off.

Wealthy isn't the word in this verse, friend. The Lord GOD says, “Exalt the lowly and bring low the exalted.” The text talks about the lowly and the exalted, not about money. God says to exalt one and bring low the other.

Yes, baker. God says, “In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you.” The sword is told to go back in its sheath, and then God says where He will judge them: right where they began. That's the text's own wording.
Edom isn't in this verse, baker. God says, “In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you.” It's all about where they came from.
That's right, baker. God ends the message with, “You will not be remembered, for I, the LORD, have spoken.” I think this is a hard one to hear. It's a sober way to end, and it's what the text says.
No ruling in this ending, baker. God's last words in the message are, “You will not be remembered, for I, the LORD, have spoken.” I think this part is heavy, and the text doesn't soften it.
